# Core exercise: More seedlings, less uncertainty?

Compare two surveys with the same observed survival proportion:

- Survey A: 2 survivors out of 5 seedlings
- Survey B: 20 survivors out of 50 seedlings

1. **Predict:** Which survey will have a narrower posterior distribution?
2. **Run:** Change only `y` and `N` in the code and compare the two posterior distributions.
3. **Explain:** Why are the posterior distributions different, even though the observed survival proportion is the same?

The code starts with Survey A. Keep the prior and grid unchanged.
If R is unavailable, compare the figures in [the result sheet](results.html).

```{r core-data-comparison, fig.height=3.4}
y <- 2
N <- 5
p <- seq(0, 1, length.out = 101)

prior <- dbeta(p, shape1 = 1, shape2 = 1) # flat prior
likelihood <- dbinom(x = y, size = N, prob = p) # likelihood
posterior <- prior * likelihood
posterior <- posterior / sum(posterior) # weights sum to 1

tibble(p = p, posterior = posterior) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = p, y = posterior)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.2, colour = "#d95f02") +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 1)) +
  labs(
    x = "Survival probability p",
    y = "Posterior probability per grid point",
    title = paste(y, "survivors out of", N, "seedlings")
  )
```
